items.name: Collect sneakers
items.about: Shoes as design, culture and memory. Every pair tells you where you were.
howToSteps: List the pairs you already own.
Pick a theme: a colour, a decade, or a sport.
Photograph each pair and note where it came from.
Wear them: a collection can be lived in.

metadata.Start with: Start with pairs you already love and wear
metadata.Where to find: Your own wardrobe, friends, sneaker meet-ups and resale groups
metadata.Care: Keep them out of direct sun; stuff with paper to hold the shape
metadata.Display idea: A clear shelf or boxes with a photo of the pair on the front

items.name: Collect watches
items.about: From your first school watch to a family heirloom, watches carry time in two ways.
howToSteps: Gather the watches you and your family already have.
Ask a repairer about any old ones.
Note who wore each one and when.
Choose a theme: hand-wound, Indian-made, or one per decade.

metadata.Start with: Start with watches already in the family
metadata.Where to find: Family drawers, local watch repairers, vintage fairs
metadata.Care: Wind or service mechanical watches; keep away from magnets and damp
metadata.Display idea: A watch roll or a tray by the window

items.name: Collect perfumes
items.about: Scents you love, samples and attars. Smelling is half the fun of collecting them.
howToSteps: Put the perfumes you own on your shelf in Scent & Perfume.
Learn the nine scent families.
Try samples before full bottles.
Log what you wear and see your favourites.

metadata.Start with: Start with what's already on your shelf
metadata.Where to find: Samples, decants, attar shops in old markets
metadata.Care: Keep bottles cool and out of sunlight; close caps tightly
metadata.Display idea: A shelf away from the window, grouped by scent family

items.name: Collect coins
items.about: India's coins change with every series. Your change jar may hold history.
howToSteps: Sort today's change by year and design.
Look for commemorative coins.
Ask elders for old coins they kept.
Note the year, mint mark and where you found it.

metadata.Start with: Start with the coins in your wallet and change jar
metadata.Where to find: Change jars, family boxes, numismatic fairs and clubs
metadata.Care: Hold by the edges; store in coin flips or albums, never clean them
metadata.Display idea: A coin album page per decade or per series

items.name: Collect banknotes
items.about: Notes show a country's art, languages and changes over time.
howToSteps: Gather leftover foreign notes from trips.
Find older Indian series at home.
Sleeve each note flat.
Note where and when each one came to you.

metadata.Start with: Start with notes from family drawers and trips abroad
metadata.Where to find: Family keepsakes, travel leftovers, collector fairs
metadata.Care: Keep flat in sleeves; don't fold, iron or tape them
metadata.Display idea: Album pages grouped by country or series

items.name: Collect stamps
items.about: Tiny artworks with a stamp of history. India Post issues beautiful commemoratives.
howToSteps: Save stamps from mail you receive.
Visit a post office philately counter.
Pick a theme so it stays manageable.
Mount them in a stockbook.

metadata.Start with: Start with stamps from letters and parcels
metadata.Where to find: Old letters, India Post philately counters, stamp clubs
metadata.Care: Use tongs; soak off paper gently; store in a stockbook
metadata.Display idea: A stockbook page per theme: birds, trains, festivals

items.name: Collect postcards
items.about: A postcard from every place you go, and maybe one to send back home.
howToSteps: Buy one postcard per new place.
Write the date and a memory on the back.
Send one to yourself or a friend.
Sort them by state as your passport grows.

metadata.Start with: Start with a postcard from your next trip
metadata.Where to find: Museum shops, post offices, local markets, trips
metadata.Care: Keep in an album or box away from damp
metadata.Display idea: A wall grid or a travel map with postcards around it

items.name: Collect fridge magnets
items.about: The easiest travel collection: small, cheap to carry and joyful on the fridge.
howToSteps: Pick one magnet per place you visit.
Prefer local crafts over generic prints.
Note the trip and date.
Arrange them by region.

metadata.Start with: Start with a magnet from your next trip
metadata.Where to find: Souvenir stalls at forts, beaches, hill stations and airports
metadata.Care: Wipe gently; keep away from screens and cards
metadata.Display idea: A fridge door, or a metal board arranged like a map

items.name: Collect keychains
items.about: Small, personal and from everywhere you've been.
howToSteps: Gather the ones lying around at home.
Add one from each trip or event.
Note who gave each one.
Hang them where you see them daily.

metadata.Start with: Start with the keychains you already have
metadata.Where to find: Souvenir shops, events, friends' trips
metadata.Care: Keep metal ones dry to avoid rust
metadata.Display idea: Hooks on a board or a jar on your desk

items.name: Collect crafts from every state
items.about: A small handmade piece from each state: Channapatna toys, Madhubani, Dhokra, Pashmina and more.
howToSteps: Find your own state's signature craft.
Buy directly from artisans when you travel.
Note the craft name, maker and village.
Aim for one from every state you stamp.

metadata.Start with: Start with something handmade from your own state
metadata.Where to find: State emporiums, crafts melas, artisans on your travels
metadata.Care: Keep textiles folded with neem leaves; dust wooden pieces
metadata.Display idea: A shelf that becomes a map of India in crafts

items.name: Collect tickets & passes
items.about: Train tickets, museum passes, gig wristbands: the paper trail of a life well lived.
howToSteps: Keep every ticket for a month.
Photograph thermal ones before they fade.
Stick them in a notebook with a memory.
Look back at the end of the year.

metadata.Start with: Start by keeping the next ticket you get
metadata.Where to find: Trains, concerts, museums, matches, films
metadata.Care: Keep thermal paper out of light; photocopy or photograph faded ones
metadata.Display idea: A scrapbook with a line about each day

items.name: Collect vinyl records
items.about: Music you can hold. Old Bollywood and classical pressings turn up in surprising places.
howToSteps: Ask family about old records.
Find a working turntable.
Collect what you'll actually listen to.
Clean records gently before playing.

metadata.Start with: Start with albums you'd listen to again and again
metadata.Where to find: Family collections, old record shops, record fairs
metadata.Care: Store upright, away from heat; hold by the edges
metadata.Display idea: Display the cover of what you're playing now

items.name: Collect comics
items.about: From Amar Chitra Katha and Tinkle to graphic novels.
howToSteps: List the comics you remember loving.
Find them in second-hand shops.
Pick a series to complete.
Read them: that's the point.

metadata.Start with: Start with the comics you grew up reading
metadata.Where to find: Old bookshops, comic cons, family shelves
metadata.Care: Bag and board them; keep away from sun and damp
metadata.Display idea: A shelf with favourite covers facing out

items.name: Collect film posters
items.about: Hand-painted and printed posters are art from Indian cinema history.
howToSteps: Choose a theme: a star, a decade, or a genre.
Look for reprints first.
Learn to spot hand-painted originals.
Frame a favourite.

metadata.Start with: Start with posters of films you love
metadata.Where to find: Poster shops, film festivals, old cinema halls
metadata.Care: Store flat or rolled in a tube; frame behind UV glass
metadata.Display idea: Rotate one framed poster on a wall

items.name: Collect signed books
items.about: Books signed by the authors you've met at festivals and readings.
howToSteps: Find an author event near you.
Bring a book you love to be signed.
Note the date and what they said.
Keep a photo of the moment.

metadata.Start with: Start with your next book festival or reading
metadata.Where to find: Literature festivals, book launches, author readings
metadata.Care: Keep spines out of sun; don't stack heavy books on top
metadata.Display idea: A special shelf for signed copies

items.name: Collect rocks & minerals
items.about: India's landscapes in your hand: agate, quartz, basalt and more.
howToSteps: Pick up a stone that catches your eye.
Look up what it might be.
Label where and when you found it.
Never take from parks or protected areas.

metadata.Start with: Start with interesting stones from your walks
metadata.Where to find: Riverbeds, hill walks, geology museums, mineral fairs
metadata.Care: Never collect in protected areas; label each stone
metadata.Display idea: Egg trays or a shadow box with labels

items.name: Collect seashells
items.about: Shells from the beaches you've walked. Take only empty shells, and only a few.
howToSteps: Take only empty shells.
Take one or two, not handfuls.
Label the beach and date.
Check local rules first.

metadata.Start with: Start with one shell from your next beach
metadata.Where to find: Beach walks (only empty shells, where allowed)
metadata.Care: Rinse in fresh water and dry; never take living shells
metadata.Display idea: A jar per beach with a little label

items.name: Collect heirloom seeds
items.about: Old local varieties of vegetables and flowers, saved and shared.
howToSteps: Save seeds from a tomato or chilli you loved.
Dry them on paper.
Label variety, date and source.
Share some with a friend.

metadata.Start with: Start by saving seeds from what you grow
metadata.Where to find: Your own garden, seed festivals, seed-saving groups
metadata.Care: Dry fully; store in paper envelopes in a cool, dark place
metadata.Display idea: Labelled envelopes in a tin

items.name: Collect die-cast model cars
items.about: Small cars, big memories. Plenty of people still have their childhood ones.
howToSteps: Find your old cars.
Pick a theme: Indian cars, race cars, or one colour.
Note where each one came from.
Display your favourite five.

metadata.Start with: Start with the cars from your childhood
metadata.Where to find: Toy shops, family boxes, collector meet-ups
metadata.Care: Dust gently; keep in cases away from sun
metadata.Display idea: A wall shelf with a little road

items.name: Collect trading cards
items.about: Cricket, football and game cards, swapped and treasured.
howToSteps: Choose a set or a team.
Swap duplicates with friends.
Sleeve your favourites.
Track which ones you're missing.

metadata.Start with: Start with cards you have or can swap with friends
metadata.Where to find: Friends, card shops, swap meets
metadata.Care: Use sleeves and a binder; keep flat and dry
metadata.Display idea: A binder page per team or set

items.name: Collect board games
items.about: Games you play with people you love. A shelf of them is a shelf of evenings.
howToSteps: Play a few at a board game café.
Get the one everyone enjoyed.
Note who you played with.
Add a new one for special occasions.

metadata.Start with: Start with one game your friends will play
metadata.Where to find: Game cafés, gifts, board game groups
metadata.Care: Keep boxes flat and sealed; bag the small pieces
metadata.Display idea: A shelf with the most-played games at eye level

items.name: Collect fountain pens
items.about: Pens that make writing slower and nicer. India has its own pen makers too.
howToSteps: Buy or inherit one pen.
Learn to fill and clean it.
Try a few ink colours.
Write a letter with it.

metadata.Start with: Start with one pen and a bottle of ink
metadata.Where to find: Old stationers, pen shows, Indian pen makers
metadata.Care: Flush with water every few weeks; keep capped
metadata.Display idea: A pen tray on your desk

items.name: Collect matchbox labels
items.about: Indian matchbox art is colourful and quirky. Collectors call it phillumeny.
howToSteps: Save every new matchbox design.
Flatten and sleeve the labels.
Group by brand or theme.
Note the town where you found it.

metadata.Start with: Start with matchboxes from around the house
metadata.Where to find: Local shops, old stock, collector groups
metadata.Care: Keep flat in an album; boxes can be flattened carefully
metadata.Display idea: Album pages by theme: animals, gods, film

items.name: Collect teas of India
items.about: A tin from each region: Darjeeling, Assam, Nilgiri, Kangra and more.
howToSteps: Note the tea you already drink.
Buy a small pack from each region.
Taste them side by side.
Write a line about each.

metadata.Start with: Start with the tea you drink every day
metadata.Where to find: Tea estates, local tea shops, travel
metadata.Care: Keep in airtight tins away from light and smells
metadata.Display idea: A row of tins with a tasting note on each

items.name: Collect building sets
items.about: Brick sets you build, display and rebuild. Many adults collect them as calm, hands-on projects.
howToSteps: Pick a theme you love: cities, space, cars, botanicals.
Build it slowly over a few evenings.
Photograph each finished build.
Keep the instructions so you can rebuild it.

metadata.Start with: Start with one set you'd love to build
metadata.Where to find: Toy stores, brand stores, second-hand sellers, gifts
metadata.Care: Keep instructions in a folder; bag loose pieces by colour
metadata.Display idea: A shelf of finished builds, rotated every few months

items.name: Collect action figures
items.about: Superheroes, film and game characters, posed and displayed.
howToSteps: Choose a universe or a character.
Decide: in the box or out of it.
Note where and when you got each one.
Pose a small scene and photograph it.

metadata.Start with: Start with a character that means something to you
metadata.Where to find: Collectible stores, comic cons, toy collector groups
metadata.Care: Keep out of direct sun; dust gently with a soft brush
metadata.Display idea: A glass shelf with a few figures posed in a scene

items.name: Collect anime figures
items.about: Figures of anime and manga characters, from small chibis to detailed scale figures.
howToSteps: Pick a favourite series.
Learn to spot authentic figures.
Start small: a chibi or a prize figure.
Note the series and character for each.

metadata.Start with: Start with a favourite character from a series you love
metadata.Where to find: Collectible stores, anime cons, online stores with authentic stock
metadata.Care: Keep the boxes; avoid sun, which fades paint
metadata.Display idea: A shelf per series with the boxes stored flat

items.name: Collect scale model kits
items.about: Build and paint model cars, planes, ships and robots from kits.
howToSteps: Start with a snap-fit beginner kit.
Read the steps before you cut a part.
Paint small parts before you assemble.
Photograph it finished.

metadata.Start with: Start with a snap-fit kit that needs no glue
metadata.Where to find: Hobby stores, model shops, online hobby sellers
metadata.Care: Keep finished models in cases away from dust
metadata.Display idea: A shelf or case with a small label for each model

items.name: Collect miniatures
items.about: Tiny worlds: dollhouse furniture, miniature food, little scenes in a box.
howToSteps: Pick a scale and stay with it.
Start a tiny scene in a box.
Add one piece at a time.
Photograph it from eye level.

metadata.Start with: Start with a small scene in a shoebox
metadata.Where to find: Hobby stores, craft stores, miniature makers online
metadata.Care: Keep in a closed case; tiny pieces get lost easily
metadata.Display idea: A shadow box that becomes a little room

items.name: Collect plush toys
items.about: Soft toys from childhood, trips and gifts, each with a story.
howToSteps: Gather the ones you already have.
Note who gave each one.
Add one from special trips.
Give them a home where you see them.

metadata.Start with: Start with the ones you already keep
metadata.Where to find: Toy stores, trips, gifts, handmade sellers
metadata.Care: Wash gently by hand; dry in shade
metadata.Display idea: A basket or a shelf where they can sit together

items.name: Collect trading card games
items.about: Cards from games like Pokemon and Magic: collected for play, art and rarity.
howToSteps: Learn to play with a starter deck.
Join a local game night.
Sleeve the cards you care about.
Track which cards you have and want.

metadata.Start with: Start with a beginner deck you can actually play
metadata.Where to find: Card and game stores, local game nights, trusted sellers
metadata.Care: Sleeve every good card; keep binders upright and dry
metadata.Display idea: A binder page per set, rarest cards in the middle

items.name: Collect finished jigsaws
items.about: Puzzles you've completed, kept as photos or glued and framed.
howToSteps: Finish one puzzle.
Photograph it complete.
Note the pieces and how long it took.
Swap finished puzzles with friends.

metadata.Start with: Start with a 500-piece puzzle of a picture you love
metadata.Where to find: Puzzle and game stores, friends swapping puzzles
metadata.Care: Store unfinished puzzles in bags inside the box
metadata.Display idea: Frame your favourite finished puzzle

items.name: Collect notebooks & journals
items.about: Notebooks and journals you love to write in, and the ones you've filled.
howToSteps: Keep every notebook you fill.
Date the first page.
Try one paper type you've never used.
Look back at an old one each year.

metadata.Start with: Start with the notebook you're using now
metadata.Where to find: Stationery stores, Indian stationery brands, gifts
metadata.Care: Keep filled notebooks upright on a shelf
metadata.Display idea: A shelf of filled notebooks, oldest to newest

items.name: Collect stickers & washi tape
items.about: Rolls of washi tape and sticker sheets for journals, letters and planners.
howToSteps: Pick a colour palette.
Use them in a journal or on letters.
Note where each set came from.
Trade stickers with friends.

metadata.Start with: Start with a few rolls you'll actually use
metadata.Where to find: Stationery stores, art stores, small Indian sticker makers
metadata.Care: Store in a flat box away from heat so the glue stays good
metadata.Display idea: A pegboard or a jar of rolls by colour

items.name: Collect art supplies
items.about: Paints, pencils, brushes and inks: the tools you love to make with.
howToSteps: List what you already have.
Try one new medium.
Make a swatch card for each set.
Keep a sketchbook of what you made with them.

metadata.Start with: Start with the colours and tools you use most
metadata.Where to find: Art supply stores, stationers, Indian art-supply brands
metadata.Care: Close paints tightly; wash and dry brushes flat
metadata.Display idea: A tray or caddy on your desk
